source.original_text: For natural d and q with 2q+1<d, let r=q+1, theta_i=(i-1/2)pi/d for i=1,...,d, and t_i=(1,sqrt(2)cos(theta_i),...,sqrt(2)cos(q theta_i)). The deterministic weighted coefficient ((r+2)/d^2) sum_i ||t_i||^2 (I_r tensor t_i t_i^T) is at most (2r(r+2)/d) I_(r^2) in positive-semidefinite order. The source uses ||t_i||^2<=2r and sum_i t_i t_i^T=d I_r.

blind_reconstruction.text:
Anonymous mathematical reconstruction

For every pair of natural numbers d,q (natural numbers include zero) satisfying
    2q + 1 < d,
make all of the following definitions within the scope of that pair d,q and that hypothesis.

Put n = q+1 as a natural number, and let r = n viewed as a real number. Thus the statement's let-bound r is real, while all index sets below have natural-number size n. Let
    D = {0,1,...,d-1},    K = {0,1,...,q}.
For each i in D, define
    θ_i = (i + 1/2)π/d.
Define the real vector t_i indexed by K by
    t_{i,0} = 1,
    t_{i,k} = sqrt(2) cos(k θ_i) for k in {1,...,q}.
The second range is empty when q=0. Define
    S_i = sum_{k=0}^q t_{i,k}^2
        = 1 + 2 sum_{k=1}^q cos^2(k θ_i),
and define the real n-by-n feature matrix F_i by
    (F_i)_{k,ℓ} = t_{i,k} t_{i,ℓ};
equivalently, F_i = t_i t_i^T.

Let N be the space of real matrices with both row and column index set K×K. An element of N is an n^2-by-n^2 matrix, with its paired indices retained explicitly. Let I_n be the identity on K, and I_{n^2} the identity on K×K. Set
    B = ((r+2)/d^2) sum_{i=0}^{d-1} S_i (I_n ⊗ F_i) in N,
    C = 2r(r+2)/d in R.
Every occurrence of d in a real denominator or coefficient means its real coercion.

Then the real matrix
    M = C I_{n^2} - B
is positive semidefinite. In full, M is symmetric and, for every real array
    x = (x_{a,k})_{(a,k) in K×K},
one has
    sum_{a,k,b,ℓ in K} x_{a,k} M_{(a,k),(b,ℓ)} x_{b,ℓ} >= 0.

Tensor ordering and the difference

The first coordinate of each paired index belongs to I_n and the second to F_i. Consequently,
    (I_n ⊗ F_i)_{(a,k),(b,ℓ)} = δ_{ab} t_{i,k} t_{i,ℓ},
    B_{(a,k),(b,ℓ)}
      = ((r+2)/d^2) δ_{ab} sum_{i=0}^{d-1} S_i t_{i,k} t_{i,ℓ},
    M_{(a,k),(b,ℓ)}
      = C δ_{ab} δ_{kℓ}
        - ((r+2)/d^2) δ_{ab} sum_{i=0}^{d-1} S_i t_{i,k} t_{i,ℓ}.
Here δ is the Kronecker delta. No flattening convention for paired indices is required or added. In a block arrangement grouped by a, B has n identical diagonal blocks and zero off-diagonal blocks.

An equivalent explicit form of the asserted quadratic-form inequality is: for every such x,
    ((r+2)/d^2)
      sum_{i=0}^{d-1} S_i sum_{a=0}^q
        (sum_{k=0}^q t_{i,k} x_{a,k})^2
    <= (2r(r+2)/d) sum_{a=0}^q sum_{k=0}^q x_{a,k}^2.
Thus the direction of the PSD difference is B <= C I_{n^2} in positive-semidefinite order.

Quantifiers, assumptions, scopes, endpoints, and dependencies

The literal quantified hypothesis is only that d,q are natural numbers and 2q+1<d. The proof parameter hq witnesses that inequality; it does not introduce an additional numerical parameter. All eight successive lets r, θ, t, S, feature, N, B, C are definitions under these quantifiers, not further assumptions and not independently chosen objects. The only final predicate is that C I_{n^2}-B is positive semidefinite. The real array x in the expanded reading is universally quantified through the meaning of positive semidefiniteness.

All finite sums cover the full indicated carriers: i=0,...,d-1, and each index of Fin(q+1) takes the values 0,...,q, including both endpoints. The natural-number hypothesis implies d>=2q+2>=2, so every division by d here has a strictly positive denominator. The angles run from θ_0=π/(2d) to θ_{d-1}=π-π/(2d), with step π/d; neither 0 nor π is a sampled endpoint.

The dimensions are n=q+1 for a feature matrix and n^2=(q+1)^2 for B, its identity, and the PSD difference. The exact prefactor of B is (q+3)/d^2, and the exact scalar bound is
    C = 2(q+1)(q+3)/d.
Both depend only on d and q. There are no implicit constants, asymptotic qualifications, auxiliary parameters, probability events, or exceptional index sets in this proposition. It does not assert that the displayed constant is optimal.

Elementary consequences, distinguished from literal assumptions

From the definitions, r>=1, r+2>0, S_i>=1, and F_i is symmetric positive semidefinite. Hence B is itself symmetric positive semidefinite; this is a deduction from its nonnegative weighted outer-product construction, not an additional hypothesis in the input. Together with the asserted conclusion this yields 0 <= B <= C I_{n^2}. Symmetry of M likewise follows already from the definitions, while the nonnegative quadratic-form condition is the substantive asserted bound.

Because (r+2)/d^2>0, the displayed quadratic-form inequality can equivalently be divided by that coefficient:
    sum_{i=0}^{d-1} S_i sum_{a=0}^q
      (sum_{k=0}^q t_{i,k} x_{a,k})^2
    <= 2rd sum_{a=0}^q sum_{k=0}^q x_{a,k}^2.
Equivalently, for A=sum_{i=0}^{d-1} S_i F_i, the assertion is A <= 2rd I_n. These are equivalent readings of the asserted conclusion, not independent input assumptions.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumCosineGram
import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Order
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Kronecker

noncomputable section
open scoped BigOperators Matrix.Norms.L2Operator
set_option autoImplicit false

/-! The deterministic weighted coefficient comparison in arXiv2610.20492v1 C.2
EGx11. The canonical cosine-frame node supplies both Gram and norm conclusions.
Original-family Gaussian transport, centering and concentration remain separate. -/
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumWeightedFrameBound

theorem actual_weighted_cosine_coefficient_bound
    {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let S : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (t i k) ^ 2
  let feature : Fin d → Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i => Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i)
  let N := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let B : N := ((r + 2) / (d : ℝ) ^ 2) •
    ∑ i : Fin d, S i • Matrix.kronecker (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) (feature i)
  let C : ℝ := 2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)
  Matrix.PosSemidef (C • (1 : N) - B) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let S : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (t i k) ^ 2
  let M := Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let N := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let feature : Fin d → M := fun i => Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i)
  let K : Fin d → N := fun i => Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (feature i)
  let α : ℝ := (r + 2) / (d : ℝ) ^ 2
  have frame := FixedSpectrumCosineGram.actual_cosine_frame_gram (d := d) (q := q) hq
  have norm_bound (i : Fin d) : S i ≤ 2 * r := by
    simpa only [r, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using frame.2.2 i
  have gram : (∑ i : Fin d, feature i) = (d : ℝ) • (1 : M) := by
    have frame_gram : t.transpose * t = (d : ℝ) • (1 : M) := frame.1
    ext j k
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin d, feature i) j k = ∑ i : Fin d, t i j * t i k :=
        Matrix.sum_apply j k Finset.univ feature
      _ = ((d : ℝ) • (1 : M)) j k := by
        simpa only [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply] using
          congrFun (congrFun frame_gram j) k
  let tensor : M →ₗ[ℝ] N :=
    (Matrix.kroneckerBilinear : M →ₗ[ℝ] M →ₗ[ℝ] N) (1 : M)
  have tensor_gram : (∑ i : Fin d, K i) = (d : ℝ) • (1 : N) := by
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin d, K i) = tensor (∑ i : Fin d, feature i) := (map_sum tensor _ _).symm
      _ = (d : ℝ) • tensor (1 : M) := by rw [gram, map_smul]
      _ = (d : ℝ) • (1 : N) := by
        change (d : ℝ) • Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (1 : M) = _
        dsimp only [Matrix.kronecker]
        rw [Matrix.one_kronecker_one]
  have K_positive (i : Fin d) : (K i).PosSemidef := by
    have F_positive : (feature i).PosSemidef := by
      simpa only [star_trivial] using Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star (t i)
    exact (Matrix.PosSemidef.one : (1 : M).PosSemidef).kronecker F_positive
  have residual_positive :
      (∑ i : Fin d, (2 * r - S i) • K i).PosSemidef :=
    Matrix.posSemidef_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ =>
      (K_positive i).smul (sub_nonneg.mpr (norm_bound i)))
  have scalar_nonnegative : 0 ≤ α := by
    exact div_nonneg (by dsimp [r]; positivity) (sq_nonneg _)
  have constant_sum :
      (∑ i : Fin d, (2 * r) • K i) = (2 * r * (d : ℝ)) • (1 : N) := by
    rw [← Finset.smul_sum, tensor_gram, smul_smul]
  have residual_identity :
      (2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)) • (1 : N) -
        α • (∑ i : Fin d, S i • K i) =
          α • (∑ i : Fin d, (2 * r - S i) • K i) := by
    simp_rw [sub_smul]
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, constant_sum, smul_sub, smul_smul]
    congr 1
    have hd : (d : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show d ≠ 0 by omega)
    dsimp [α]
    field_simp
  change ((2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)) • (1 : N) -
    α • (∑ i : Fin d, S i • K i)).PosSemidef
  rw [residual_identity]
  exact residual_positive.smul scalar_nonnegative

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumWeightedFrameBound

candidate_publication_context.statement: The weighted cosine coefficient is bounded by \(\frac{2r(r+2)}d I_{r^2}\). The truncated Gaussian row templates satisfy the same bound after summing their marginal second moments.
assumptions: Let \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), and \(r=q+1\). Thus \(d\ge2\), \(r\ge1\), and \(q=0\) is included.
For source rows \(i=1,\ldots,d\), put \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(t_i[0]=1\), and \(t_i[k]=\sqrt2\cos(k\theta_i)\) for \(1\le k\le q\). Lean uses source index \(i.val+1\).
Write \(S_i=\|t_i\|^2=\sum_{k=0}^q t_i[k]^2\) and \(F_i=t_it_i^\top\). All matrices are real, and paired tensor indices put the Gaussian/identity coordinate first and the feature coordinate second.

For the consumer only, \(Z\) has the canonical standard Gaussian probability law \(\gamma_r=N(0,I_r)\) on real Euclidean space, \(R=\|Z\|^2\), and \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\). The cutoff is the closed event \(R\le L\).

The square is ordinary matrix multiplication. Every \(Y_i^2\) is proved Bochner integrable in the Euclidean operator norm. Each integral is a marginal expectation against \(\gamma_r\), with no retained-mass normalization.
The order \(\preceq\) means that the upper-minus-lower matrix is positive semidefinite. No Gram, norm, moment, integrability or order certificate is an extra hypothesis.

steps.title: Reuse the exact cosine frame
steps.text: The existing canonical frame theorem supplies both the feature squared-length bound and the Gram identity. Rewrite the Gram entries as a finite sum of outer products, then tensor by the identity to obtain the paired-coordinate identity. The signed high-frequency Gram conclusion is unused in this estimate.
steps.lean:
have frame := FixedSpectrumCosineGram.actual_cosine_frame_gram (d := d) (q := q) hq
  have norm_bound (i : Fin d) : S i ≤ 2 * r := by
    simpa only [r, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using frame.2.2 i
  have gram : (∑ i : Fin d, feature i) = (d : ℝ) • (1 : M) := by
    have frame_gram : t.transpose * t = (d : ℝ) • (1 : M) := frame.1
    ext j k
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin d, feature i) j k = ∑ i : Fin d, t i j * t i k :=
        Matrix.sum_apply j k Finset.univ feature
      _ = ((d : ℝ) • (1 : M)) j k := by
        simpa only [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply] using
          congrFun (congrFun frame_gram j) k
  let tensor : M →ₗ[ℝ] N :=
    (Matrix.kroneckerBilinear : M →ₗ[ℝ] M →ₗ[ℝ] N) (1 : M)
  have tensor_gram : (∑ i : Fin d, K i) = (d : ℝ) • (1 : N) := by
    calc
      (∑ i : Fin d, K i) = tensor (∑ i : Fin d, feature i) := (map_sum tensor _ _).symm
      _ = (d : ℝ) • tensor (1 : M) := by rw [gram, map_smul]
      _ = (d : ℝ) • (1 : N) := by
        change (d : ℝ) • Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (1 : M) = _
        dsimp only [Matrix.kronecker]
        rw [Matrix.one_kronecker_one]

steps.title: Expose a nonnegative weighted residual
steps.text: Each identity-tensored feature outer product is PSD. The norm bound makes every residual weight nonnegative. Sum these PSD matrices and multiply by the nonnegative exact scalar. The standing range gives the nonzero denominator needed for the final normalization.
steps.lean:
have K_positive (i : Fin d) : (K i).PosSemidef := by
    have F_positive : (feature i).PosSemidef := by
      simpa only [star_trivial] using Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star (t i)
    exact (Matrix.PosSemidef.one : (1 : M).PosSemidef).kronecker F_positive
  have residual_positive :
      (∑ i : Fin d, (2 * r - S i) • K i).PosSemidef :=
    Matrix.posSemidef_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ =>
      (K_positive i).smul (sub_nonneg.mpr (norm_bound i)))
  have scalar_nonnegative : 0 ≤ α := by
    exact div_nonneg (by dsimp [r]; positivity) (sq_nonneg _)
  have constant_sum :
      (∑ i : Fin d, (2 * r) • K i) = (2 * r * (d : ℝ)) • (1 : N) := by
    rw [← Finset.smul_sum, tensor_gram, smul_smul]
  have residual_identity :
      (2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)) • (1 : N) -
        α • (∑ i : Fin d, S i • K i) =
          α • (∑ i : Fin d, (2 * r - S i) • K i) := by
    simp_rw [sub_smul]
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, constant_sum, smul_sub, smul_smul]
    congr 1
    have hd : (d : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show d ≠ 0 by omega)
    dsimp [α]
    field_simp
  change ((2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)) • (1 : N) -
    α • (∑ i : Fin d, S i • K i)).PosSemidef
  rw [residual_identity]
  exact residual_positive.smul scalar_nonnegative

steps.title: Use the canonical fourth matrix moment
steps.text: Set up the actual Gaussian row templates and fixed continuous linear tensor maps. The existing radial fourth matrix theorem supplies integrability of RZZ transpose and its exact mean. Its integrability is transported to each untruncated square template W_i. This fold includes the complete private statement and setup.

steps.title: Square the truncated templates exactly
steps.text: Use the two rank-one square identities, Kronecker multiplication and indicator idempotence. Thus Y_i squared is the closed-event indicator times W_i. The event is measurable and W_i is integrable, giving integrability of every actual square. Each W_i is a nonnegative multiple of the tensor vector outer product and is PSD.
steps.lean:
-- Exact rank-one and tensor squares retain one cutoff indicator.
  have rank_square (v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ) :
      Matrix.vecMulVec v v * Matrix.vecMulVec v v =
        (∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (v k) ^ 2) • Matrix.vecMulVec v v := by
    rw [Matrix.vecMulVec_mul_vecMulVec, Matrix.vecMulVec_smul]
    congr 1
    simp [dotProduct, pow_two]
  have gram_square (x : E) : G x * G x = R x • G x := by
    have h := rank_square (WithLp.ofLp x)
    have radius_sum : (∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (x k) ^ 2) = R x :=
      (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq x).symm
    simpa only [radius_sum] using h
  have feature_square (i : Fin d) : feature i * feature i = S i • feature i :=
    rank_square (t i)
  have squared_as_indicator (i : Fin d) : squared i = good.indicator (W i) := by
    funext x
    by_cases hx : x ∈ good
    · simp only [squared, Y, Set.indicator_of_mem hx]
      change ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (G x) (feature i)) *
        ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (G x) (feature i)) =
          c i • Matrix.kronecker (R x • G x) (feature i)
      dsimp only [Matrix.kronecker]
      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, ← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul,
        gram_square x, feature_square i]
      ext a b
      change (d : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ *
        ((R x * G x a.1 b.1) * (S i * feature i a.2 b.2))) =
          c i * ((R x * G x a.1 b.1) * feature i a.2 b.2)
      dsimp [c]
      simp only [div_eq_mul_inv]
      ring
    · simp [squared, Y, Set.indicator_of_notMem hx]
  have squared_integrable (i : Fin d) : Integrable (squared i) μ := by
    rw [squared_as_indicator i]
    exact (W_integrable i).indicator good_measurable
  have W_positive (i : Fin d) (x : E) : (W i x).PosSemidef := by
    let v : Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun a => x a.1 * t i a.2
    have rank_positive : (Matrix.vecMulVec v v).PosSemidef := by
      simpa only [star_trivial] using Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star v
    have W_rank : W i x = (c i * R x) • Matrix.vecMulVec v v := by
      ext a b
      change c i * (R x * (x a.1 * x b.1) * (t i a.2 * t i b.2)) =
        (c i * R x) * ((x a.1 * t i a.2) * (x b.1 * t i b.2))
      ring
    rw [W_rank]
    exact rank_positive.smul (mul_nonneg
      (div_nonneg (Finset.sum_nonneg (fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _)) (sq_nonneg _))
      (sq_nonneg ‖x‖))

steps.title: Integrate the aggregate PSD residual
steps.text: At every row and point, W_i minus Y_i squared is either zero or W_i. Sum these PSD residuals. Both finite sums are integrable. Prove that the finite-dimensional real PSD cone is closed and convex, then integrate the aggregate residual inside that cone.
steps.lean:
-- Integrate the whole PSD residual sum, with integrability for every square.
  have residual_positive (x : E) :
      ((∑ i : Fin d, W i x) - ∑ i : Fin d, squared i x).PosSemidef := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    apply Matrix.posSemidef_sum Finset.univ
    intro i _
    rw [squared_as_indicator i]
    by_cases hx : x ∈ good
    · simpa [Set.indicator_of_mem hx] using (Matrix.PosSemidef.zero : (0 : N).PosSemidef)
    · simpa [Set.indicator_of_notMem hx] using W_positive i x
  have W_sum_integrable : Integrable (fun x => ∑ i : Fin d, W i x) μ :=
    integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => W_integrable i)
  have squared_sum_integrable : Integrable (fun x => ∑ i : Fin d, squared i x) μ :=
    integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => squared_integrable i)
  have PSD_closed : IsClosed {A : N | A.PosSemidef} := by
    have hermitian_closed : IsClosed {A : N | A.IsHermitian} := by
      change IsClosed {A : N | star A = A}
      exact isClosed_eq continuous_star continuous_id
    have quadratic_closed (v : (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) → ℝ) :
        IsClosed {A : N | 0 ≤ dotProduct (star v) (Matrix.mulVec A v)} := by
      apply isClosed_le continuous_const
      change Continuous (fun A : N => ∑ a, star (v a) * ∑ b, A a b * v b)
      fun_prop
    convert hermitian_closed.inter (isClosed_iInter quadratic_closed) using 1
    ext A
    simp [Matrix.posSemidef_iff_dotProduct_mulVec]
  have PSD_convex : Convex ℝ {A : N | A.PosSemidef} := by
    intro A hA B hB a b ha hb hab
    exact (hA.smul ha).add (hB.smul hb)
  have integrated_residual :
      (∫ x, (∑ i : Fin d, W i x) - ∑ i : Fin d, squared i x ∂μ).PosSemidef :=
    PSD_convex.integral_mem PSD_closed (Filter.Eventually.of_forall residual_positive)
      (W_sum_integrable.sub squared_sum_integrable)

steps.title: Evaluate the sum and apply the deterministic producer
steps.text: Transport the exact radial fourth mean through each fixed tensor map and commute the finite sum with integration. This gives the aggregate upper matrix B_coeff. Add its integrated PSD residual to the deterministic producer residual. At q=0 the feature is one-dimensional and the bound remains the valid source value 6/d.
steps.lean:
have W_mean (i : Fin d) : (∫ x, W i x ∂μ) = α • (S i • K i) := by
    calc
      (∫ x, W i x ∂μ) = scaled i (∫ x, weighted x ∂μ) :=
        (scaled i).integral_comp_comm moment.1
      _ = scaled i ((r + 2) • (1 : M)) := congrArg (scaled i) moment.2
      _ = α • (S i • K i) := by
        change c i • Matrix.kronecker ((r + 2) • (1 : M)) (feature i) =
          α • (S i • Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (feature i))
        dsimp only [Matrix.kronecker]
        rw [Matrix.smul_kronecker, smul_smul, smul_smul]
        congr 1
        dsimp [c, α]
        simp only [div_eq_mul_inv]
        ring
  have W_sum_mean : (∫ x, ∑ i : Fin d, W i x ∂μ) = B := by
    rw [integral_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => W_integrable i)]
    simp_rw [W_mean]
    exact Finset.smul_sum.symm
  rw [integral_sub W_sum_integrable squared_sum_integrable, W_sum_mean,
    integral_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => squared_integrable i)] at integrated_residual
  have deterministic := actual_weighted_cosine_coefficient_bound (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change (C • (1 : N) - B).PosSemidef at deterministic
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (squared i) μ) ∧
    (C • (1 : N) - ∑ i : Fin d, ∫ x, squared i x ∂μ).PosSemidef
  refine ⟨squared_integrable, ?_⟩
  convert deterministic.add integrated_residual using 1
  abel

end AutoSamplingTheory.Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumWeightedFrameBound
